name: round-3a-ai-error-taxonomy
purpose: Conservative AI-art and coloring-page source QA checklist for blocking questionable source images before production processing.
automaticDetectionLimit: This taxonomy guides heuristics and manual review artifacts. It is not a claim that anatomy or AI-art defects can be detected perfectly by automation.
decisionPolicy: When uncertain, reject for now. Rejected images may only be restored by an explicit future approval/update manifest.

issueFamilies.round3aHandling: Human-adjacent categories are rejected for now unless later explicitly approved, because Round 3A does not perform manual anatomy review.

items: asymmetric wings where symmetry is expected
impossible creature structure unless clearly stylized and intentional
issueFamilies.round3aHandling: Automation can only flag indirect risks such as broken silhouettes, clutter, or crop issues. Ambiguous animal anatomy should be rejected in later manual review.

items: line clutter that makes coloring difficult
random extra shapes that do not belong
visible watermark, signature, username, logo, or text remnants
overly dense detail with no clear colorable regions
important subject parts too close to the edge
inconsistent decorative elements such as mismatched earrings, buttons, bows, clothing seams, jewelry, ornaments, or accessories
details that look polished at a glance but do not make sense when inspected
issueFamilies.round3aHandling: Heuristics flag crop risk, dense detail, border-heavy linework, many tiny components, duplicate filenames, non-PNG files, and unreadable files.

items: tiny enclosed areas that would be frustrating to color
output likely to feel unprofessional to a user
issueFamilies.round3aHandling: Heuristics reject very faint, over-dense, cluttered, low-margin, or low-resolution sources.

reviewArtifactPolicy: Rejected review versions are copied under pipeline/review/source-qa for local inspection and remain ignored by Git.
